response.sql: WITH oc AS (SELECT o.account_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM "order" o GROUP BY o.account_id) SELECT oc.account_id, d.A3 AS region, oc.order_count, oc.order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count * 1.0) FROM oc) AS diff_from_avg FROM oc JOIN account a ON a.account_id = oc.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id ORDER BY diff_from_avg DESC, oc.account_id ASC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Region is district.A3 of the account's branch district (account.district_id), not the client's district.
Ties at the 10th rank are cut off by LIMIT 10, with account_id as the tiebreaker, so exactly 10 rows are returned.
The average is the mean order count per account across accounts that have at least one order, computed as a non-integer (unrounded) value.
